headline: India Reaffirms Suspension Of Indus Water Treaty Amid SCO Meeting
metaDescription: India has stated its position on the Indus Water Treaty remains unchanged following a visit by a Pakistani minister to an SCO forum held in New Delhi.
aiSummaryBullets: India maintains that its stance regarding the Indus Water Treaty has not shifted.
The government suspended the long-standing agreement in 2025 as a response to security concerns.
The statement followed the participation of a Pakistani minister in an SCO forum hosted in India.
aiContextParagraph: The Indus Water Treaty was suspended by the Indian government in 2025. This action was taken as a punitive measure following the April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam, which resulted in the deaths of 26 individuals. The recent diplomatic interaction occurred as a Pakistani minister visited Delhi to attend a meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). Despite this high-level forum attendance, Indian officials have formally clarified that there is no modification to the existing suspension of the water-sharing agreement. The treaty, which historically managed the distribution of water from the Indus River system between the two nations, remains a central point of contention in bilateral relations. Tensions between the two countries have remained heightened since the 2025 security incident, leading to ongoing diplomatic adjustments and public reaffirmations of policy positions regarding regional stability and cross-border agreements.
whyItIsViral: This story is currently being covered by two independent news outlets as officials address treaty status during an international diplomatic gathering.
